notes.meaning: A person who pulls away from others often does so to chase his own selfish desires. He rejects wise advice and sets himself against sound judgment. God designed people to live and learn together in community rather than in stubborn isolation.
A fool has no real interest in understanding the truth. His only goal in conversation is to broadcast his own thoughts and show off. He loves to hear himself talk rather than learn what is right.

When an ungodly person enters a room, scorn and disrespect usually follow him. Wicked behavior always drags disgrace and shame along with it. Those who mock God end up bringing dishonor on themselves and those around them.

The words of a wise person run deep like clear, quiet water that never dries up. Wisdom flows out of a good heart like a fresh, bubbling brook. This kind of speech brings constant refreshment and help to everyone who listens.

It is completely wrong for a judge to favor an evil person because of wealth or power. It is just as evil to deny justice to an innocent person. Leaders and judges must examine the facts of a case rather than the status of the person.

A fool uses careless speech that stirs up arguments and practically begs for physical punishment. His mouth causes his own ruin, trapping his very soul in misery. Ungoverned talk brings painful consequences directly onto the speaker's own head.

Gossip and whispered secrets seem like delicious snacks that people swallow eagerly. But like poisoned treats, they sink deep into the listener's heart and leave lasting wounds. Talebearing breaks up close friendships and spreads suspicion everywhere.

A person who is lazy in his work is closely related to someone who deliberately destroys property. One person wastes things through neglect, while the other ruins them on purpose. Both paths lead to poverty and spiritual ruin.

The name of the Lord stands for His character, His power, and His faithful promises. Godly people run to Him in prayer and faith, finding complete safety like someone sheltered inside a high fortress. God lifts those who trust Him far above danger.

A wealthy person often treats his money like a fortified city that can keep him safe from harm. But that high defensive wall exists only in his own imagination. Earthly riches give a false sense of security and fail when real trouble strikes.

A proud heart is a sure sign that a sudden downfall is near. On the other hand, true humility prepares a person to receive honor from God and others. We should stay humble so that pride does not lead to our ruin.

Giving an answer before listening to the whole matter is foolish and humiliating. People who rush to speak show that they are conceited instead of wise. We need the patience to hear all the facts before forming a conclusion.

A courageous human spirit can hold a person up through physical illness and hard trials. But when the spirit itself is broken by grief or a guilty conscience, all strength is gone. Only God can comfort and sustain a crushed soul.

Sensible people know they do not have enough wisdom yet, so they keep looking for more. Their ears listen carefully to wise teaching, and their hearts welcome the truth. Gaining knowledge is an ongoing habit for anyone who is truly wise.

Giving a generous gift can open doors and bring a person into the presence of great leaders. Polite generosity helps remove barriers and clears a path to higher positions. Practical courtesy can help a person advance in life.

differ.view: Adam Clarke viewed this custom as a corrupt, degrading practice where gifts act like bribes to gain access to powerful rulers.
Some commentators apply this verse to a person's God-given talents and abilities making room for them to serve others.

notes.meaning: The first person to tell his side of a dispute always sounds convincing. But when his opponent steps up and cross-examines him, the real facts come to light. Good judges never make up their minds until they have heard both sides.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Latin translations read this to mean that a righteous man accuses himself first, which was used to teach the confession of sins.

notes.meaning: Casting lots in ancient times was a way to let God settle difficult arguments. This practice stopped angry quarrels and kept powerful rivals from fighting with swords. Handing hard disputes over to the Lord brings peace when words fail.

When an offended brother has been wronged, winning him back is harder than capturing a walled city. Quarrels between close friends lock up hearts like the heavy iron bars of a castle gate. We should take great care never to hurt those closest to us.

A person's inner life is filled with the harvest of what comes out of his mouth. Just as good food satisfies the stomach, wise and upright speech brings peace to the heart. We inevitably taste the good or bad results of the words we speak.

The tongue has the power to do great good or cause terrible harm, leading either to life or death. A person's words can save, heal, and encourage, or they can destroy reputations and kill. Anyone who talks freely must be ready to live with the fruit of what he says.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some popular modern teachers claim this verse gives believers the supernatural ability to speak physical things, health, or wealth into existence.

notes.meaning: Finding a wife is finding a true blessing and receiving a special token of the Lord's favor. Marriage provides companionship and helps a person walk with God. A faithful marriage should be received with deep thanksgiving to the Lord.

differ.view: Adam Clarke taught that marriage itself is a blessing ordained by God, so finding any wife is generally better than remaining single.
John Gill emphasized that the verse specifically means finding a good, virtuous wife, because only a godly spouse brings this divine blessing.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Ancient Greek and Latin translations add a line stating that divorcing a good wife casts away happiness, while keeping an unfaithful wife is foolish.

notes.meaning: A poor man is humbled by his need and speaks with gentle pleas for mercy. A rich man, however, is often made proud by his wealth and responds with harsh words. God warns the prosperous not to let their money make them unkind to those in need.

Having a large crowd of superficial companions can easily bring a person to ruin. But a true, loyal friend will stay closer and prove more reliable than a blood brother. A single devoted friend is worth far more than many casual acquaintances.

differ.view: Charles Spurgeon taught that the friend who stays closer than a brother directly refers to Jesus Christ, the Savior of sinners.
Adam Clarke argued that the text has no reference to Christ, but is strictly a proverb about the value of loyal human friendship.
